meta.title: GPT-6.1 Sol · AI/ML · solo · run 1
meta.note: Main run, 60 minutes. The verifier accepted 6 of 8 credited claims; 3 set a new best held-out result on their dataset. Verdicts from the re-run of the official verifier.

artifacts.title: A compact residual classifier with Cutout and flip averaging for CIFAR-10
artifacts.summary: A pre-activation residual network is trained with random reflected crops, horizontal flips, and zero-valued square masking in normalized image space. The public-data experiment uses a fixed random train/validation split; the checkpoint is retained for inference-only verification. Validation results are development evidence, not a claim about the unseen official test set. The comparison arm without square masking is also released. Architecture and all optimization choices are in run.py; predict.py only loads weights and predicts.
artifacts.reason: accepted: hidden error rate: model beats the environment baseline (difference -0.0157, 95% CI [-0.0196, -0.0115], beyond the minimum effect 0.0012)

claim.statement: The released compact residual classifier with Cutout and horizontal-flip logit averaging improves CIFAR-10 error over the supplied prediction reference.

artifacts.title: Complementary word and character margin models for AG News
artifacts.summary: The method combines a word unigram/bigram TF-IDF linear SVM with a character TF-IDF linear SVM by averaging per-document standardized decision scores. A fixed stratified validation split was used for development. The matched comparator uses the same word TF-IDF representation and logistic regression. Exploratory alternatives, including class log-count weighting, are recorded rather than omitted. This contribution tests the released fitted model against its matched fitted comparator; it does not assert a new state of the art or treat validation as the unseen official test set.
artifacts.reason: accepted: hidden error rate: arm a beats the other arm (difference -0.0128, 95% CI [-0.0168, -0.0084], beyond the minimum effect 0.0019)

claim.statement: Combining word and character linear margin classifiers lowers AG News classification error relative to a matched word TF-IDF logistic-regression classifier.

artifacts.title: Horizontal-flip logit averaging improves a fixed CIFAR-10 residual classifier
artifacts.summary: This isolates an inference-time intervention: average class logits for the original image and its horizontal reflection, with no retraining. Both completed training arms improved on the same public validation split. The verification compares the exact same Cutout checkpoint with and without flip averaging. Only development errors are reported; unseen official-test performance remains to be measured.
artifacts.reason: accepted: hidden error rate: arm a beats the other arm (difference -0.0041, 95% CI [-0.0067, -0.0016], beyond the minimum effect 0.0010)

claim.statement: Horizontal-flip logit averaging reduces classification error relative to single-view inference for the released Cutout-trained CIFAR-10 classifier.

artifacts.title: Exploratory AG News model-selection record and unsuccessful class weighting
artifacts.summary: The initial recorded text experiment compared word TF-IDF logistic regression, word linear SVMs, character linear SVMs, and one-versus-rest Naive-Bayes log-count-ratio SVMs. Binary-count NB weighting did not improve the matched validation split; the word/character combination did. This is an exploratory observation, not a preregistered equivalence or general negative claim. The full candidate metrics, code, fitted models, and validation decision scores are retained in the evidence run. Later requests that failed to save metrics are not used as quantitative evidence. Validation-guided selection is a limitation, and the final scored tests use the untouched evaluator articles.
artifacts.reason: not credited: notes are never credited

artifacts.title: Linear margin training improves AG News over matched logistic regression
artifacts.summary: This comparison holds the word unigram/bigram TF-IDF representation fixed and changes the classifier and its regularization setting. It compares LinearSVC against the supplied style of logistic baseline. Development gains appeared on both recorded stratified splits. The isolated paired inference run confirms the second split. Verification uses the corresponding all-public-data refits, never hidden labels. This is a practical recipe comparison, not a claim that hinge loss dominates optimally tuned logistic regression.
artifacts.reason: accepted: hidden error rate: arm a beats the other arm (difference -0.0104, 95% CI [-0.0134, -0.0072], beyond the minimum effect 0.0019)

claim.statement: The released word TF-IDF linear SVM recipe reduces AG News error relative to its matched logistic-regression recipe.

artifacts.title: Cutout and Mixup models have complementary CIFAR-10 errors
artifacts.summary: Two matched compact residual models differ in training augmentation: square masking versus convex image/target mixing. Averaging their flip-averaged logits improves over the Cutout member. The validation comparison is paired and uses the same image split. This is evidence for diversity ensembling, not evidence that one augmentation dominates the other. The same weights and inference-only comparison are released.
artifacts.reason: accepted: hidden error rate: arm a beats the other arm (difference -0.0049, 95% CI [-0.0071, -0.0028], beyond the minimum effect 0.0009)

claim.statement: Averaging the released Cutout and Mixup classifiers reduces CIFAR-10 error relative to the Cutout classifier alone.

artifacts.title: A longer cosine schedule improves the compact Cutout image classifier
artifacts.summary: The architecture, seed, public validation split, augmentation family, optimizer, and inference averaging are held fixed. The longer schedule stretches cosine decay rather than continuing from the short-run checkpoint. The longer run improves validation error, with paired inference verifying both checkpoints. This single-seed result is a schedule comparison, not a universal scaling law. A separate all-public-data refit is released in the associated recorded run; its training-subset errors are not validation evidence.
artifacts.reason: accepted: hidden error rate: arm a beats the other arm (difference -0.0039, 95% CI [-0.0069, -0.0009], beyond the minimum effect 0.0009)

claim.statement: The longer cosine training schedule reduces CIFAR-10 error relative to the shorter schedule for the released Cutout residual classifier.

artifacts.title: All-public-data word/character TF-IDF margin ensemble for AG News
artifacts.summary: Final all-public-data refit of the sparse text recipe. It uses word unigram/bigram and character TF-IDF linear SVMs, averaging per-document standardized decision scores. The second split supports an improvement over matched logistic regression but not a decisive incremental benefit over the word SVM. The final prediction test compares directly against the evaluator reference, with no fitting on evaluation inputs. Earlier exploratory model variants and their limitations are retained in the research report.
artifacts.reason: rejected: did not replicate on hidden data by the minimum effect: difference -0.0050, 95% CI [-0.0084, -0.0016], needed below -0.0017

claim.statement: The released all-public-data sparse word/character margin ensemble improves AG News error over the supplied logistic-regression prediction reference.

artifacts.title: Synthesis, unsuccessful variants, and validation limitations
artifacts.summary: The reproducibility report separates three relatively clear effects—word margin training versus matched logistic regression, image reflection averaging, and complementary image-model averaging—from weaker observations. The Cutout-versus-standard training difference was not decisive; character features did not decisively beat a strong word SVM on the second split; the small neural text model did not improve the sparse ensemble. A longer image training schedule helped the fixed validation split. All-data image refits retain misleadingly named monitoring metrics on a former validation subset; those are training-subset diagnostics and are explicitly excluded from generalization claims. Selection and paired-test multiplicity, single-seed image evidence, and extra ensemble compute are acknowledged. The attached report maps these limitations to the published methods and tests.
artifacts.reason: not credited: notes are never credited

artifacts.title: All-public-data compact Cutout/Mixup ensemble for CIFAR-10
artifacts.summary: Final prediction package combining the all-public-data Cutout and Mixup residual-network refits. Each model uses horizontal-reflection logit averaging, then the two model logits are averaged. The split-trained experiments support the architecture, longer schedule, inference reflection averaging, and augmentation diversity; they do not provide a direct validation estimate of these final all-data weights. The all-data runs report training-subset monitoring errors, which are explicitly not used as generalization evidence. Verification is inference-only on untouched evaluator inputs. Extra translated views were tested and omitted because their incremental validation improvement was not convincing. This package consolidates the earlier component findings rather than claiming a new architecture.
artifacts.reason: rejected: claimed numbers do not reproduce within 10% on rerun

claim.statement: The released all-public-data residual ensemble improves CIFAR-10 classification error over the supplied prediction reference.

artifacts.title: Additional split robustness for the AG News margin-model recipe
artifacts.summary: Additional stratified splits reproduce the direction of the word TF-IDF SVM versus matched logistic-regression gain. These splits overlap and are not independent repetitions; the result is descriptive support for the existing finding, not a new scored claim. No hyperparameters were changed between these checks. The recorded run contains every per-split error and paired test.

artifacts.title: Regularization control for the AG News logistic comparator
artifacts.summary: A late control varied logistic-regression regularization over a broad range while retaining the same text split and TF-IDF representation. Tuning improved the logistic comparator, narrowing the gap, but the fixed SVM recipe retained a lower validation error than every tested setting. This is exploratory validation evidence, not an optimally tuned universal loss comparison. It supports the recipe-level wording of the earlier finding and highlights that part of the original gain came from regularization choice.

artifacts.title: Final prediction packages and evaluator-contract verification
artifacts.summary: The final AG News package is method-65b286a3; the final CIFAR-10 package is method-2f52c2f1. Earlier method artifacts retain development checkpoints and should not be interpreted as additional independent discoveries. A server-run contract audit exercised the actual evaluator-facing inference branches on temporary label-free public inputs, confirming model loading, input paths, ID preservation, class ranges, and prediction-file columns. This audit establishes executability only, not unseen-data accuracy. The final all-data smoke-test errors are training-subset diagnostics and are not performance claims. The component comparison findings remain separately interpretable because each changes a specific training or inference choice.

events.text: I’ll inspect the experiment protocol, datasets, and baselines before choosing a tractable research question.
I’ll identify the baseline strength and data formats, then prioritize improvements that can be trained and independently retested within the time limit.
I need the untruncated baseline and dataset details to choose the first experiment.
I’ll pursue two tractable directions: robust sparse text classification and augmentation for a compact image classifier. First I’ll verify available libraries and hardware through a recorded run.

The text baseline is a linear bag-of-ngrams model, so complementary character features and class-aware feature weighting are promising. I’ll also start a compact CIFAR training run while CPU text experiments proceed.
I’ll test whether supervised term weighting and character n-grams improve AG News classification on a fixed stratified validation split, retaining the fitted models for later verification.
For images, I’ll compare standard crop-and-flip training with Cutout under matched initialization, data split, and optimization. A compact wide residual network should make both arms feasible.
The first jobs are running. I’ll check their status and prepare a clean inference path so any successful model can be tested without retraining.
I’ll make the text inference script support both the baseline comparison and the combined word/character classifier, with no fitting on hidden inputs.
The main experiments are in flight. I’ll check whether execution is serialized and inspect the schema example before preparing publication records.

The first text run favors complementary word and character SVMs; the Naive Bayes weighting did not help. I’ll inspect job progress and use the next CPU experiment to test whether that ensemble gain survives a second split.
Before scheduling more training, I’ll check GPU utilization and prepare the second text split. This will distinguish a repeatable feature-combination effect from validation-set selection.

I’ll test a more controlled version of class-aware weighting: apply log-count ratios to normalized TF-IDF rather than unnormalized binary counts. This checks whether the earlier negative result was due to document-length sensitivity.

The server is serializing the queued runs. While the image experiment trains, I’ll prepare final text inference and a diagnostic that measures paired errors rather than relying only on aggregate accuracy.

The data contains headline/body structure and recurring newswire markers. I’ll prepare a focused text experiment to test whether headline emphasis adds useful information beyond ordinary word and character features.
The first image run has finished, so I’ll inspect its recorded results and let the matched Cutout arm complete before drawing conclusions.

The standard image model is already below the reference error on validation. I’ll fix file-versus-directory checkpoint loading and prepare paired significance diagnostics for the augmentation comparison.
I’ll use the remaining compute for a stronger final image model and a distinct regularization test. Mixup provides a useful comparison because it changes targets as well as images, unlike Cutout.

The image runs are fast enough to support a stronger final model. For text, I’ll prepare one focused feature-capacity experiment to test whether longer character contexts and joint training improve on score averaging.
Cutout reduced validation error, especially with flip averaging, but the gain is modest. I’ll quantify paired uncertainty and train a longer all-data model for the stronger prediction test.
Some CPU jobs remain queued while later GPU jobs start. I’ll inspect execution status to ensure the text experiments are actually scheduled and avoid wasting the remaining session.
I’ll download the completed checkpoints for a reproducible package and inspect their storage footprint. The final tests will load recorded weights rather than retrain.
I’ll isolate image inference from training and verify flip averaging as a separate, low-cost intervention. Its held-out test will compare the same checkpoint with and without averaging.
I’ll check the current queue and completed records before adding any more experiments; the next decisions should depend on the pending text replications and image comparison.
I’ll preserve the current image result as a complete reproducible package, then use the remaining time to strengthen its evidence and final model rather than risk leaving only unfinished runs.

Mixup and Cutout are similar on this validation split, so I won’t claim one universally dominates the other. I’ll test whether a longer Cutout schedule improves the same architecture and retain a stronger all-data checkpoint.

I’ll test one nonlinear text model as a complementary view. A deep averaging network over word and bigram embeddings may capture interactions missed by linear classifiers, but it will need to earn its place on validation.
One queued request timed out, and the capacity run reported no saved outputs despite completing its calculations. I’ll investigate the recording issue before relying on those results.

I’ll avoid further queue congestion and publish the reproducible text comparison already supported by a complete recorded run. The claim will be limited to the combined feature model versus its matched word-only logistic baseline.
Concurrent requests appear to be causing long waits and incomplete output capture. I’ll stop adding jobs, inspect the active run’s directory layout, and switch to strictly sequential execution.
I’ll check whether queued experiments inherited the intended output directories. Missing metrics must be resolved before those runs can support any claim.
The active run has the correct isolated environment. I’ll let it finish, then verify saved outputs before doing any additional training.
I’ll consolidate the remaining text work into one self-contained run: fit on a validation split, record paired diagnostics, then refit the selected word/character models on all public articles.
The longer all-data image run is near its expected completion. I’ll wait for the current queue to drain so the final text run and inference checks can execute without overlap.

The all-data checkpoint is saved; its reported “validation” errors are actually training-subset errors and will not be used as generalization evidence. I’ll now queue the final text fit and a compact analysis of the genuinely held-out image predictions.

Horizontal-flip averaging improved both completed image models on the fixed validation split. I’ll publish it as a separate inference-only comparison, keeping the checkpoint fixed so the evaluator isolates the averaging effect.
I’ll prepare a standalone negative-result note for the class-weighted text model, while keeping it separate from scored claims because it lacks preregistered equivalence testing.
The final image validation run should finish shortly. I’ll inspect all completed records, then run a single foreground verification to confirm the prediction scripts and checkpoint mounts.

The paired analysis supports flip averaging and suggests complementary Cutout/Mixup errors, while the Cutout-versus-standard training gain remains uncertain. I’ll inspect the text replication and verify the strongest image checkpoint in a foreground run.
The stronger checkpoint reproduces the flip-averaging benefit with a clear paired improvement. I’ll now verify the diversity ensemble and collect a clean comparison of training schedules.

The second text split confirms a clear gain over logistic regression but not a clear gain over the word SVM alone. I’ll isolate that loss-function comparison and verify the all-data inference package before publishing the final text result.

I’ll publish the cleanly isolated effects: margin loss versus logistic loss for text, complementary augmentation ensembling for images, and a longer image training schedule. Each test will load fixed recorded models.
I’ll check whether existing contributions can be updated, then run one final model-combination analysis. The goal is a stronger final predictor, not duplicate claims.

The neural text model did not beat the sparse models, so I’ll leave it out. I’ll analyze the retained prediction files for useful complementary features and test the final all-data packages without touching hidden labels.

The text diagnostics show no compelling gain from the extra neural or headline models. I’ll keep the simpler text predictor and use the remaining GPU time for an all-data Mixup refit, enabling a final diversity ensemble with the saved Cutout model.

I’ll prepare a more thorough image inference check: averaging translated views as well as reflections. This is inexpensive relative to training and may reveal whether crop invariance remains a source of error.

I’ll package the final all-data predictors separately from validation experiments. The final report will distinguish robust effects from exploratory ones and explicitly exclude training-subset errors from performance claims.
I’ll publish the final text refit and a synthesis note now. The text test will compare against the evaluator’s own reference predictions, rather than only our matched local baseline.
The final image refit is still training. I’ll preserve the synthesis report and wait before running the last smoke tests, avoiding the concurrent-output issues encountered earlier.

I’ll run the final text inference check in the foreground once the active refit releases the executor. This checks that the published all-data model loads and writes the required prediction files; its public-data accuracy is not held-out evidence.

Extra translated views did not give a convincing gain, so the final image predictor will use only reflection averaging and the two complementary models. I’ll verify the all-data ensemble’s output contract and publish it without treating its training-subset diagnostics as validation.
The final packages are published and load correctly. I’ll use the remaining time for additional text splits to check whether the margin-model gain is stable beyond the two development splits.

The margin-model improvement held across the additional text splits. I’ll attach this as supporting evidence and audit the earlier inference script so every published comparison matches its recorded recipe.

The audit confirms that the initial text comparison uses the same character model as its recorded ensemble metric. I’ll finish with an independent image-training seed to check whether reflection averaging helps another fitted model.

A fresh image training run would not finish reliably in the remaining time. Instead, I’ll check an important text confound: whether tuning logistic-regression regularization removes the apparent margin-model advantage.

Logistic tuning narrows but does not eliminate the margin-model advantage on this split. I’ll publish that control as a limitation-aware supplement, then audit the contribution contracts one last time.
I’ll test the exact evaluator-facing branches using temporary label-free input files. This verifies paths, IDs, row counts, and prediction formats independently of the self-test branches.
Both final predictors pass the label-free input/output audit. I’ll publish the verification record and identify the final packages so they are not confused with earlier development checkpoints.

The final models, component findings, controls, and limitations are published. Both prediction packages pass the input/output contract audit; unseen-data performance remains for the evaluator to determine.
